sections.h2: Who sells in Calumet City, and how
sections.html:
Sellers in Calumet City include longtime owners, landlords, heirs and people holding houses that sat empty. The 2020 census found about one in ten housing units vacant, and owners live in 55.7 percent of units, a lower share than in most nearby suburbs.

That mix produces three common routes: a listing handled by an agent, a sale you manage yourself, and a direct sale to a cash buyer who accepts repairs and tenants as they come. A listing suits an updated house, and a cash buyer suits a house a lender would balk at. Each route needs the city's transfer stamp and a paid final water bill.

sections.h2: Home values and what they mean for costs
sections.html:
A typical Calumet City home is worth $145,200 for 2020 through 2024, and typical gross rent is $1,177. Middle household income is $55,369, there are 14,332 households, and the one-way commute is 34.4 minutes. The 2020 count was 36,033 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 34,798, which is 3.5 percent below the 2020 base.

At these prices, flat costs such as the transfer stamp and the final water bill take a bigger bite out of proceeds than they would on a costlier house. Price against closed sales within a few blocks of yours instead of a metro-wide number. Higher vacancy means your house competes with empty units on the same blocks, and a clean, inspected house stands out most in that kind of market.

The clerk's Real Estate Transfer Declaration prints $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and the same for the seller, which totals $8.00 per $1,000 or part thereof. The form is written for transfers up to and including $2 million.

  • Collect the stamps at least 48 hours ahead and leave about half an hour for processing.
  • Only certified checks, money orders or cash are taken.
  • Whoever requests the stamp must be the owner of record, an attorney or a broker, and an agent writes a bar or license number on the form.
  • An exempt transfer cites a paragraph of Sec. 82-323 of the municipal code and submits a copy of the deed.

The City Clerk's office answers at (708) 891-8110, Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. The form lists Thornton Township and ZIP code 60409 for the property.

sections.h2: Final water bill and utility charges
sections.html:
Every outstanding water bill has to be paid before a property is sold. The seller or the seller's representative orders a final meter reading at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought. Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 to schedule it.

Monthly utility rates, Utilities Ordinance 26-01
ChargeRate
Water$11.45 per 1,000 gallons
Sewer$1.33 per 1,000 gallons
Stormwater$2.00 per 1,000 gallons or part thereof
Refuse$31.30 per unit, or $15.65 for a first unit at age 65

Water rates move automatically with any increase from Chicago or Hammond. The water comes entirely from Lake Michigan. A new owner files a water service application, and some accounts require a deposit.

The city's Forms and Applications page lists a rental application, an annual rental code compliance letter, an owner-occupied form, a Crime Free Housing licensing application and a vacant and foreclosed property registration. A landlord selling a rental should confirm that the application and the compliance letter are current, because a buyer's attorney tends to ask for them.

Ask Building and Zoning, (708) 891-8120, whether the vacant and foreclosed registration applies to your house and whether any permit or violation is open on the address. The same page offers permit forms for building, electrical, plumbing, HVAC and fences, and an overhead sewer rebate program form. A quick call before you accept an offer avoids surprises after the inspection.

Cook County's Clerk runs the Recordings Division, which keeps office hours from 9 to 5 and accepts its last customer at 4:45. Buyer and seller also complete the PTAX-203 Illinois declaration.

The state levies its own tax of 50 cents per $500. Home rule municipalities may add theirs, and Calumet City's stamp falls into that category. For the property tax proration, exemptions appear as deductions on the second installment bill, so ask the County Treasurer for the amounts and due dates on your parcel.

Three city numbers cover most of a handover: the clerk at (708) 891-8110, Water Billing at (708) 891-8121 and Public Works at (708) 891-8161. Call them in that order if you want the stamp price, the meter reading and any street or utility question settled before the closing date.

Buyers often compare Calumet City with houses in Hammond, Lansing, Dolton and South Holland, so state commute and highway access in a listing. A cash buyer comfortable with tenants in place, an older furnace or an overhead sewer can often close faster than a buyer who needs a loan, while a retail buyer pays more for a house that has been updated.

sections.h2: Order of steps at the city
sections.html:
Start with the final meter reading, since it has the longest lead time. Once the water account is closed out and paid, bring the signed declaration and the payment to the clerk at least 48 hours before you need the stamps. Allow about half an hour at the counter. If the transfer is exempt, cite the paragraph of Sec. 82-323 and bring a copy of the deed.

If an agent handles the stamp for you, make sure the form shows the agent's bar or license number. A form that comes back incomplete can cost you the extra days you did not budget for.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or empty house
sections.html:
Heirs often inherit a house that has sat empty. Start by confirming who is the owner of record, because only the owner, an attorney or a broker can request the stamp. Then ask Building and Zoning about the vacant and foreclosed registration and any open violation, order the final meter reading, and collect any permit records. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as-is can close without waiting on a lender's inspection list.

Keep copies of everything you submit to the city, along with the receipts, so the title company can match each payment on the settlement statement. If a buyer asks about the rental or vacancy forms, tell them what you filed and when, and hand over the paperwork right away, in writing if possible.

faqs.q: What is the Calumet City transfer stamp price?
faqs.a: The clerk's form lists $4.00 per $1,000 or part thereof for the buyer and $4.00 for the seller, $8.00 in total per $1,000 or part thereof, for transfers up to and including $2 million.

faqs.q: How is a final water reading ordered in Calumet City?
faqs.a: Call Water Billing at (708) 891-8121. The city asks for the order at least 48 hours before the stamp is bought, and all water bills must be paid before the sale.

faqs.q: What payment does the stamp office accept?
faqs.a: Certified check, money order or cash only. Plan to pick the stamps up at least 48 hours ahead.

faqs.q: Which office records a Calumet City deed?
faqs.a: The Cook County Clerk's Recordings Division, because the city is in Cook County. It takes customers until 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a rental house in Calumet City be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The city has a rental application and an annual compliance letter, so confirm both are in order and ask Building and Zoning at (708) 891-8120 about open permits before signing a contract.
